sites_https_justification: All project sites are served over HTTPS: the GitLab project https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr , the pkgdown site https://bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/raddr/ and the CRAN page https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=raddr . The GitHub copy (github.com/bart-turczynski/raddr) is a read-only mirror, also HTTPS-only.
description_good_justification: DESCRIPTION and README give a clear, succinct description of what raddr does (report what an IP address literal means under each standard and classify it against the IANA special-purpose registries): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr#readme
interact_justification: The pkgdown site https://bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/raddr/ explains how to obtain the package (README installation section), links the bug tracker ("Report a bug") and the contributing guide (https://bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/raddr/CONTRIBUTING.html).
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) explains how to report bugs and request features in the GitLab issue tracker, that changes are sent as merge requests on GitLab (the GitHub repository is a read-only mirror), and what a merge request needs: tests for new code, one NEWS.md bullet per user-facing change, and a passing verification command (sh data-raw/verify.sh).
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states what a contribution must pass: the single verification chain data-raw/verify.sh (floor drift, lintr, spelling, R CMD check --as-cran with error_on = "warning"), and that man/ is generated from roxygen comments, which are edited instead of the .Rd files: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
license_location_justification: DESCRIPTION declares License: MIT + file LICENSE, and the LICENSE file (the CRAN MIT template's year and copyright holder) is at the repository top level: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/blob/main/LICENSE
floss_license_osi_justification: MIT is an OSI-approved open source license: https://opensource.org/license/mit
documentation_basics_justification: Basic documentation ships in the README and three vignettes (introduction, edge cases, reason codes), published on the pkgdown site https://bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/raddr/ and rendered by CRAN: https://CRAN.R-project.org/web/packages/raddr/vignettes/introduction.html
documentation_interface_justification: Every exported function is documented with roxygen2 man pages, published as the reference at https://bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/raddr/reference/ and by CRAN as the reference manual: https://CRAN.R-project.org/web/packages/raddr/raddr.pdf
repo_public_justification: Public GitLab repository: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr . The GitHub repository is a read-only mirror.
repo_track_justification: All changes are tracked in git: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/commits/main
repo_interim_justification: Interim development commits are publicly available on GitLab between releases: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/commits/main
repo_distributed_justification: Uses git, a distributed version control system: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr
version_unique_justification: Each release carries a unique version (DESCRIPTION Version; CRAN refuses a version it already has): https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=raddr . Development builds carry a .9000 suffix (main is 0.1.2.9000).
version_semver_justification: Uses semantic-style x.y.z versioning (0.1.0, 0.1.1, 0.1.2); release tags at https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/tags
version_tags_justification: Releases are tagged in git (v0.1.0, v0.1.1, v0.1.2): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/tags . v0.1.2 is the commit submitted to CRAN.
release_notes_justification: NEWS.md documents user-facing changes for each release: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/blob/main/NEWS.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerabilities have been fixed to date; NEWS.md records all changes: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/blob/main/NEWS.md
report_tracker_justification: GitLab work items serve as the public issue tracker: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/work_items
report_process_justification: Users submit bug reports through the GitLab issue tracker (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/work_items), linked as "Report a bug" on the pkgdown site https://bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/raddr/ . DESCRIPTION names the same tracker as BugReports by its legacy /-/issues address, the form R's CRAN incoming check requires.
report_responses_justification: No bug report has been filed on the public tracker to date (0 issues on 2026-10-03), so none is unacknowledged: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/work_items
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement request has been filed on the public tracker to date (0 issues on 2026-10-03), so none is unanswered: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/work_items
report_archive_justification: GitLab Issues provide a publicly available, searchable archive of reports and responses: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/work_items/?state=all
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: The vulnerability-reporting process is published in the security policy, which CONTRIBUTING.md points reporters to: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md . Reports go to the maintainer by email, with a confidential GitLab issue as a documented alternative; it states the supported versions, a 7-day acknowledgement target, coordinated disclosure, and what is in and out of scope.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: SECURITY.md (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md) documents two confidential channels: email to bartek@turczynski.pl, and a GitLab issue submitted with "This issue is confidential" ticked, visible only to the reporter, assignees and project members allowed to see confidential issues.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received through GitLab in the last 6 months (0 issues, confidential ones included, on 2026-10-03), so none has waited more than 14 days: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/work_items
build_justification: Builds with the standard R toolchain (R CMD build / INSTALL, devtools); pure R, no compiled code: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr
build_common_tools_justification: Uses the standard, widely available R build tooling.
build_floss_tools_justification: R and its toolchain are free/open source software: https://www.r-project.org/
test_justification: Automated test suite using testthat (edition 3), including WPT URL-test corpus, libc oracle fixtures and hedgehog property tests: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/tree/main/tests/testthat
test_invocation_justification: Tests run with testthat::test_local() or devtools::test(), and as part of R CMD check; the full gate is sh data-raw/verify.sh: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/blob/main/data-raw/verify.sh
test_most_justification: Coverage is measured with covr; a local covr::package_coverage() run on 2026-10-03 (commit 498bb8f) measured 97.8% line coverage. No CI job measures or publishes coverage: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
test_policy_justification: The policy is informal and applied in practice: nearly every R/ source file has a tests/testthat/test-*.R counterpart, and behavioral commits ship with tests (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/tree/main/tests/testthat). It is not written down in CONTRIBUTING.md.
tests_are_added_justification: New functionality and fixes ship with tests; recent behavioral commits on main (e.g. the vctrs floor fix, the exported policy seams) each add or change tests/testthat files: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/commits/main
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) does not state that a change must add or update tests.
warnings_justification: lintr and R CMD check --as-cran surface warnings in data-raw/verify.sh (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/blob/main/data-raw/verify.sh), which runs as the pre-push hook and in the check:linux-release CI job on every push to main (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml).
warnings_fixed_justification: The verification chain fails on any lint and on any R CMD check warning, so warnings are fixed before a push lands.
warnings_strict_justification: data-raw/verify.sh fails on any lintr finding and runs rcmdcheck with error_on = "warning": https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/blob/main/data-raw/verify.sh
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer applies secure design principles; raddr treats every literal as untrusted, performs no network access, and reports facts (all readings and reason codes) rather than allow/deny verdicts, leaving policy to the caller.
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer knows the IP-literal parsing pitfalls behind SSRF bypasses (octal/hex/short-form IPv4, inet_aton vs inet_pton divergence, IPv6 zone IDs, transition embeddings) and tests them against browser (WPT) and libc oracles.
crypto_password_storage_justification: raddr stores no passwords or credentials.
crypto_random_justification: raddr does not generate security-sensitive random values.
crypto_tls12_justification: raddr does not establish network connections.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: raddr does not establish network connections.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: raddr does not establish network connections.
delivery_mitm_justification: Distributed via CRAN and GitLab over HTTPS; CRAN publishes per-package checksums: https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=raddr
delivery_unsigned_justification: All distribution downloads are served over HTTPS (CRAN, GitLab); no hash is retrieved over plain HTTP: https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=raddr
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No outstanding known vulnerabilities; tracker at https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/work_items
static_analysis_justification: lintr runs a full-package lint (.lintr, aligned with goodpractice::gp()'s linter set) as a blocking step of data-raw/verify.sh, in the pre-push hook and the check:linux-release CI job: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/blob/main/data-raw/verify.sh
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: lintr and R CMD check find defects but are not vulnerability scanners, and no vulnerability-focused analyzer or dependency audit runs over raddr.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: The verification chain fails on any lintr finding, so static-analysis findings are fixed before a push lands.
static_analysis_often_justification: lintr runs on every push: data-raw/verify.sh is the pre-push hook, and the check:linux-release CI job runs it again on every push to main: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
dynamic_analysis_justification: Generator-driven property testing with hedgehog (randomized inputs with shrinking: totality, round-trip and order axioms) in tests/testthat/test-property.R (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/blob/main/tests/testthat/test-property.R), plus a seeded random-byte totality sweep in test-invariants.R, runs in R CMD check in the check:linux-release CI job on every push to main, so before every release.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: raddr is pure R with no compiled code (no src/ directory), so it contains no memory-unsafe code.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: raddr's testthat expectations (expect_*) are assertions checked at runtime on every run of the verification chain and the check:linux-release CI job: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/tree/main/tests/testthat
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: A failing property or invariant test fails the verification chain, so any finding is fixed before a push lands; none is open.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: The GitLab CI pipeline (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/pipelines) runs the full verification chain (lintr, spelling, R CMD check --as-cran with the testthat suite) in check:linux-release on every push to main and on release tags, plus the citation and BugReports checks (configuration: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml). Branch pushes and merge requests start no pipeline; the same chain runs as a pre-push hook on every branch.
discussion_justification: GitLab Issues provide a public forum for project discussion: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/work_items
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials are committed. A gitleaks scan of the full git history (204 commits across all refs, 2026-10-03) found no leaks: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr
english_justification: Documentation and issue-tracker interaction are conducted in English (Language: en-US): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr#readme
hardening_justification: Hardening mechanisms (e.g. HTTP security headers, compiler hardening flags) apply to web applications and compiled code; raddr is a pure-R library.
sites_password_security_justification: Project sites (GitLab, CRAN) manage their own authentication; raddr operates no site with user passwords.
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: CRAN release 0.1.2 (2026-09-21) and frequent commits on main: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/raddr/-/commits/main
